summary.text: Michael S. Cashman is the incumbent Democratic and Working Families Party candidate for New York State Assembly District 115 in the November 3, 2026 general election.
He was elected to the seat in a November 2025 special election after nearly a decade as Town Supervisor of the Town of Plattsburgh.

paragraphs.text: Cashman is a first-generation college graduate and two-time SUNY Plattsburgh alumnus, according to his official biography.

He served nearly a decade as Town Supervisor of the Town of Plattsburgh, where he became the youngest person elected to the position, and advanced projects including the town's Water and Wastewater Capital Plan, the Battlefield Memorial Gateway and the CHAMP Law on housing.

He serves on the SUNY Plattsburgh University Council, received the National TRIO Achiever Award from the Council for Opportunity in Education in 2024, and has chaired the New York State Commission on National and Community Service.
Cashman was elected in a November 2025 special election to represent the 115th Assembly District, which includes Clinton and Franklin counties and portions of Essex County.
He chairs the Task Force on New York Canada Relations and is a member of the Aging, Agriculture, Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, and Small Business committees, among others.

His official biography lists housing, health care, education, infrastructure, broadband and cell service, and support for farmers and small businesses among his focus areas, and says he lives in the Town of Plattsburgh.
